params.name: aero_case
params.rationale: The OpenFOAM case, against the project root. Each gate copies it into its own scratch and runs there; nothing is written into case/.

params.name: aero_geometry
params.rationale: The body's surface file, in the OpenFOAM install. It is part of the OpenFOAM tutorials (GPL-3.0-or-later, its origin before OpenFOAM not stated), so it is never copied into this Apache-2.0 repository: the gates copy it into their scratch only. A copy under the project was the rejected alternative.

rejected.why: GPL-3.0-or-later with its origin not stated; this repository is Apache-2.0

params.name: aero_geometry_sha256
params.rationale: The sha256 of motorBike.obj.gz in ESI OpenFOAM v2606 (measured on 2026-10-23). Another file at the same path is an error naming both digests: the drag area is of this body, by content.

params.name: aero_body_group
params.rationale: The patch group snappyHexMesh puts the body's 67 regions in (the tutorial's `inGroups`): the drag is summed over it, and the pictures draw it.

params.name: aero_u_inf_m_s
params.rationale: m/s: R1's 72 km/h. The air comes to the bike at this speed in the model; on the road the bike moves through still air at it, the same flow seen from the bike. The case's inlet says (20 0 0), and aero.reference holds the two equal.

params.name: aero_ref_length_m
params.rationale: m: the tutorial's own reference length (its forceCoeffs `lRef`, the wheelbase), used for the Reynolds number only: Re = 20 x 1.42 / 1.5e-5 = 1.9e6, past the 5e5 aero.regime asks for turbulent wall layers. The drag area needs no length. What lost is in PARAMS.

rejected.why: the body's length in x, nose to the rear tyre; the wheelbase is the tutorial's and is what a reader of OpenFOAM's case compares with

params.name: aero_sound_speed_m_s
params.rationale: m/s: the ISA sea-level speed of sound (15 degC), for the Mach number: 20 / 340.3 = 0.059, far below the 0.3 past which the incompressible solver would not hold. The air's viscosity is the tutorial's, nu 1.5e-5 m^2/s in case/constant/transportProperties (ISA sea level: 1.46e-5).

params.name: aero_ranks
params.rationale: MPI ranks for each parallel run. The machine the demo was measured on has 7 physical cores, and other work shares it: 6 leaves one. The pack's default is 8 (with --oversubscribe). The ranks move the time, and the mesh and the drag area a little (about 1e-6 of it, the pack's DEFAULT_RANKS note): the pack decomposes with `hierarchical`, so one mesh on one rank count gives one history.

rejected.why: the tutorial's count; on 7 physical cores it needs --oversubscribe, and with other work on the machine each rank waits for a core

params.name: aero_iter_unc_max_pct
params.rationale: % of the mean drag area: the largest iterative uncertainty U_I = (max - min) / 2 over the last 100 iterations that aero.converged accepts (the author's choice, design decision D3: common practice for RANS verification). Measured on the tutorial's base mesh: 0.24% at iteration 1500 (2026-10-23). On this project's meshes at iteration 500 (2026-10-25): 0.603% on the base mesh (358654 cells), and 1.98% on the ladder's finest (2674337 cells), which fails C7 before any GCI is computed.

params.name: aero_rho_kg_m3
params.rationale: kg/m^3: ISA sea-level air (15 degC, 101 325 Pa), R1's "still sea-level air". aero.drag_area reports the drag force with it, F_D = 0.5 rho U^2 CdA (0.35 m^2 is about 86 N at 20 m/s); no gate judges a force, and the drag area itself needs no density (the solver's pressure is kinematic).

params.name: aero_ladder_ratio
params.rationale: The mesh ladder's ratio: each level's background block is 1.5 times finer in every direction, (32 16 12), (48 24 18), (72 36 27), and snappyHexMesh refines every cell with it. The tutorial's own ladder at 1.5 gave effective ratios 1.42 and 1.37 from its cells (2026-10-23), past the 1.3 Celik et al. 2008 ask. What lost is in PARAMS.

rejected.why: Celik's example ratio; the finest mesh of the motorBike would hold about 22 million cells, past the pack's cap of 20 million
the effective ratio from the cells comes out under 1.3 (P0's box: 1.25 and 1.29), and the ladder fails before it solves

params.name: aero_gci_max_pct
params.rationale: % of the finest mesh's drag area: the largest mesh error band (GCI) aero.mesh_independence accepts (the author's choice, design decision D3: common practice for RANS verification). This project's ladder ran on 2026-10-25 (500 iterations a level, 6 ranks): 0.29925, 0.29625 and 0.30206 m^2 on 358654, 926215 and 2674337 cells, which does not converge in one direction, and its finest mesh did not settle under 1% (U_I 1.98%). So no GCI is computed, and C7 reads Failing whatever this number is, first for the level that did not settle. P0's ladder of the tutorial's own case (its box, block (20 8 8) and 1500 iterations a level, 2026-10-23) did the same (0.3075, 0.2964, 0.3007 m^2; U_I 1.09% on its finest).

rejected.why: the pack's selftest baseline states it for its spheroid, whose band at the formal order is 15.7%; a drag area known to 20% does not answer R1's 0.35 m^2

params.name: aero_timeout_s
params.rationale: s each OpenFOAM tool may run before it is stopped with every rank, and the gate skips. The longest single run is the ladder's finest solve. P0's finest tutorial mesh (2.6 million cells) took 5613 s for 1500 iterations on 8 ranks, and this base mesh's 500 iterations took about 6 min on 6 ranks (2026-10-23): about an hour for the finest level's 500 on 6 ranks. This project's finest level (2674337 cells) took 1587 s for its 500 on 6 ranks (2026-10-25), and the whole ladder 3256 s. Three hours leaves room for a machine shared with other work, so only a hung rank reaches it. What lost is in PARAMS.

rejected.why: measured on the base mesh only; the finest level's solve is estimated at about an hour on 6 ranks, so an hour would stop a healthy run and the ladder would read Skipped, not judged

fail.hint: an evaluator failed the current design, a physical result failed, or an evaluator's value does not meet the claim's acceptance condition

pass.hint: every evaluator is qualified and passed on the current inputs, inside its operating context, and every value compared with the acceptance condition meets it — checked does not mean true

pending.hint: an evaluator of the claim is unrun on the current inputs

refuted.hint: an evaluator failed the current design, a physical result failed, or an evaluator's value does not meet the claim's acceptance condition

stale.hint: a pass whose read set has changed since, or whose prerequisite is invalidated or unrun: nothing is checked now

unclaimed.hint: no evaluator, none qualified, one unqualified, or one outside its operating context; or an assumption nobody owns

unverified.hint: waits on an article: no physical result yet, or a pass no article binds to the current inputs
